predecessors.name: Duchy of Lotharingia
predecessors.text: Lower Lotharingia: Belgium without Crown Flanders (West Flanders and East Flanders west of the Scheldt), Luxembourg, the Netherlands and the Rhineland around Aachen and Cologne

successors.name: Duchy of Brabant
successors.text: Flemish Brabant, Walloon Brabant, Antwerp and most of North Brabant

ledger.x: 959: Bruno divides Lotharingia and Lower Lorraine is born.
977: Otto II enfeoffs Charles, the exiled younger brother of King Lothair of France, with Lower Lorraine; a Carolingian prince holds the duchy.
980: the bishops of Liège gain secular powers.
1012: Godfrey I (the page's Godfrey II) becomes duke, the first of the dukes the page lists with reign years.
1024: the bishops of Utrecht become princes of the Empire.
1033: Gothelo I reunites Lower and Upper Lorraine.
1044: Upper Lorraine is separate again; Gothelo II holds Lower Lorraine 1044-1046.
By 1059: Flanders takes the imperial lands west of the Schelde.
1087: Godfrey of Bouillon becomes duke (1087-1100) and later leads the First Crusade; Henry IV enfeoffed Henry of Limburg in 1100 and Henry V installed Godfrey I of Leuven in 1106.
1096: the Bishopric of Liège takes the Duchy of Bouillon.
1106: the house of Leuven (Louvain) takes the duchy.
1190: the title passes to Brabant and the duchy loses its territorial authority.

certainty.note: The pages give no border for the duchy; the regions are modern countries and circles around Aachen and Cologne.
